constellations.And: Andromeda, the chained princess of Greek myth rescued by Perseus. Home of the Andromeda Galaxy (M31).
constellations.Ant: Antlia, the Air Pump: a faint figure created by Lacaille in the 1750s to honour the vacuum pump.
constellations.Aps: Apus, the Bird of Paradise, a southern bird added from the Dutch navigators' voyages of the 1590s.
constellations.Aqr: Aquarius, the Water-Bearer: an ancient zodiac figure pouring a stream of water, linked to Ganymede in Greek myth.
constellations.Aql: Aquila, the Eagle that carried Zeus's thunderbolts. Altair is its brightest star.
constellations.Ara: Ara, the Altar on which the gods swore an oath before their war with the Titans.
constellations.Ari: Aries, the Ram with the Golden Fleece sought by Jason and the Argonauts.
constellations.Aur: Auriga, the Charioteer, carrying brilliant Capella and the little kids on his arm.
constellations.Boo: Boötes, the Herdsman, driving the Great Bear around the pole. Home of orange Arcturus.
constellations.Cae: Caelum, the Chisel (or Graving Tool), a faint figure created by Lacaille in the 1750s.
constellations.Cam: Camelopardalis, the Giraffe: a dim northern figure introduced by Plancius around 1612.
constellations.Cnc: Cancer, the Crab that Hera sent against Heracles. Contains the Beehive Cluster (M44).
constellations.CVn: Canes Venatici, the Hunting Dogs held on a leash by Boötes. Home of the Whirlpool Galaxy (M51).
constellations.CMa: Canis Major, the Great Dog following Orion. It holds Sirius, the brightest star in the night sky.
constellations.CMi: Canis Minor, the Little Dog, led by Procyon, its brightest star.
constellations.Cap: Capricornus, the Sea-Goat, one of the oldest recognised constellations, with roots in Babylonian sky lore.
constellations.Car: Carina, the Keel of the old ship Argo Navis. It holds Canopus and the great Carina Nebula.
constellations.Cas: Cassiopeia, the vain queen whose W-shape circles the north pole opposite the Big Dipper.
constellations.Cen: Centaurus, the wise centaur Chiron. It holds Alpha Centauri, the nearest star system to the Sun.
constellations.Cep: Cepheus, king of Aethiopia and father of Andromeda. Delta Cephei gave its name to Cepheid variables.
constellations.Cet: Cetus, the sea monster sent to devour Andromeda. Home of the pulsating variable Mira.
constellations.Cha: Chamaeleon, the Chameleon, a small southern figure from the Dutch voyages of the 1590s.
constellations.Cir: Circinus, the Compass, one of Lacaille's instruments-of-science constellations.
constellations.Col: Columba, the Dove, said to be the bird Noah released. Named by Plancius in 1592.
constellations.Com: Coma Berenices, the hair of Queen Berenice II, offered to the gods for her husband's safe return.
constellations.CrA: Corona Australis, the Southern Crown, a delicate arc of stars known since Ptolemy.
constellations.CrB: Corona Borealis, the Northern Crown, said to be the jewelled crown of Ariadne.
constellations.Crv: Corvus, the Crow, sent by Apollo to fetch water and delayed by a fig tree.
constellations.Crt: Crater, the Cup of Apollo, set on the back of Hydra beside Corvus.
constellations.Cru: Crux, the Southern Cross: the smallest of the 88 constellations and a time-honoured navigation guide.
constellations.Cyg: Cygnus, the Swan, flying down the Milky Way. Its brightest stars form the Northern Cross.
constellations.Del: Delphinus, the Dolphin that carried Poseidon's bride Amphitrite back to him.
constellations.Dor: Dorado, the Goldfish (the dolphinfish), holding most of the Large Magellanic Cloud.
constellations.Dra: Draco, the Dragon slain by Heracles, coiling around the north pole. Thuban was once the pole star.
constellations.Equ: Equuleus, the Little Horse, the second smallest constellation, beside Pegasus.
constellations.Eri: Eridanus, the great river winding from Orion's foot deep into the south, ending at Achernar.
constellations.For: Fornax, the Furnace, a Lacaille chemistry apparatus. It holds a rich cluster of galaxies.
constellations.Gem: Gemini, the twins Castor and Pollux, brothers of Greek myth and patrons of sailors.
constellations.Gru: Grus, the Crane, a southern bird added by Dutch navigators in the 1590s.
constellations.Her: Hercules, the strongman of Greek legend. Home of the great globular cluster M13.
constellations.Hor: Horologium, the Pendulum Clock, Lacaille's tribute to Huygens's invention.
constellations.Hya: Hydra, the many-headed water serpent: the largest of the 88 constellations.
constellations.Hyi: Hydrus, the Lesser Water Snake of the far south, a figure from the Dutch voyages.
constellations.Ind: Indus, the Indian, a southern figure from the Dutch navigators' era.
constellations.Lac: Lacerta, the Lizard, a small zigzag between Cygnus and Andromeda.
constellations.Leo: Leo, the Lion slain by Heracles. The Sickle marks its head and Regulus is its heart.
constellations.LMi: Leo Minor, the Little Lion, a faint figure added by Hevelius in 1687.
constellations.Lep: Lepus, the Hare, crouched at Orion's feet.
constellations.Lib: Libra, the Scales, once the claws of Scorpius and later the Roman balance of justice.
constellations.Lup: Lupus, the Wolf, held up by the Centaur in Greek star lore.
constellations.Lyn: Lynx, named by Hevelius because you would need a lynx's eyes to see its faint stars.
constellations.Lyr: Lyra, the lyre of Orpheus. Vega, its brightest star, was once the pole star and will be again.
constellations.Men: Mensa, the Table Mountain, named by Lacaille for the peak above Cape Town. The only constellation named for a place.
constellations.Mic: Microscopium, the Microscope, one of Lacaille's science-instrument constellations.
constellations.Mon: Monoceros, the Unicorn, lying across the winter Milky Way beside Orion.
constellations.Mus: Musca, the Fly, a small southern constellation from the Dutch navigators.
constellations.Nor: Norma, the Carpenter's Square, one of Lacaille's instrument constellations.
constellations.Oct: Octans, the Octant. It contains the south celestial pole.
constellations.Oph: Ophiuchus, the Serpent-Bearer, the healer Asclepius wrestling a great snake.
constellations.Ori: Orion, the mighty hunter, with Betelgeuse, Rigel and the three belt stars. Home of the Orion Nebula (M42).
constellations.Pav: Pavo, the Peacock, a southern figure from the Dutch voyages, bird of Hera.
constellations.Peg: Pegasus, the winged horse of Greek myth. Its Great Square is an autumn signpost.
constellations.Per: Perseus, the hero who slew Medusa. Holds the Double Cluster and the eclipsing variable Algol, the Demon Star.
constellations.Phe: Phoenix, the mythical bird reborn from its ashes. Home of the bright southern star Ankaa.
constellations.Pic: Pictor, the Painter's Easel, a Lacaille figure of the 1750s.
constellations.Psc: Pisces, the Fishes, tied by a cord: Aphrodite and Eros escaping the monster Typhon.
constellations.PsA: Piscis Austrinus, the Southern Fish, anchored by lonely Fomalhaut.
constellations.Pup: Puppis, the Stern of the Argo Navis, rich in open clusters along the Milky Way.
constellations.Pyx: Pyxis, the Mariner's Compass, a faint figure carved from the old ship Argo.
constellations.Ret: Reticulum, the Reticle, named for the eyepiece grid used to measure star positions.
constellations.Sge: Sagitta, the Arrow, one of the smallest constellations.
constellations.Sgr: Sagittarius, the Archer aiming at Scorpius. It points toward the centre of our galaxy.
constellations.Sco: Scorpius, the Scorpion that killed Orion, marked by red Antares.
constellations.Scl: Sculptor, a Lacaille figure. It contains the south galactic pole.
constellations.Sct: Scutum, the Shield of Sobieski, named by Hevelius for the Polish king.
constellations.Ser: Serpens, the only constellation in two parts: the head (Caput) and the tail (Cauda), held by Ophiuchus.
constellations.Sex: Sextans, the Sextant used by Hevelius to measure star positions.
constellations.Tau: Taurus, the Bull. It carries the Pleiades, the Hyades and bright red Aldebaran.
constellations.Tel: Telescopium, the Telescope, Lacaille's tribute to the instrument.
constellations.Tri: Triangulum, a small northern triangle. Home of the Triangulum Galaxy (M33).
constellations.TrA: Triangulum Australe, the Southern Triangle, noted by Dutch navigators.
constellations.Tuc: Tucana, the Toucan. Home of the Small Magellanic Cloud and the globular 47 Tucanae.
constellations.UMa: Ursa Major, the Great Bear. Its seven brightest stars form the Big Dipper.
constellations.UMi: Ursa Minor, the Little Bear, with Polaris, the North Star, at the tip of its tail.
constellations.Vel: Vela, the Sails of the old ship Argo Navis, with a famous supernova remnant.
constellations.Vir: Virgo, the maiden of the harvest, holding bright Spica and facing the Virgo galaxy cluster.
constellations.Vol: Volans, the Flying Fish, another southern figure from the Dutch navigators.
constellations.Vul: Vulpecula, the Little Fox. Home of the Dumbbell Nebula (M27).

messierNotes.1: The Crab Nebula: the remnant of the supernova that Chinese astronomers recorded in 1054.
messierNotes.3: A globular cluster of roughly half a million stars.
messierNotes.8: The Lagoon Nebula, a glowing stellar nursery visible to the naked eye.
messierNotes.11: The Wild Duck Cluster, one of the richest and most compact open clusters.
messierNotes.13: The Great Hercules Cluster: about 300,000 stars, and the target of the 1974 Arecibo message.
messierNotes.16: The Eagle Nebula, home of the Pillars of Creation.
messierNotes.17: The Omega (or Swan) Nebula, a bright star-forming region.
messierNotes.20: The Trifid Nebula, split in three by dark dust lanes.
messierNotes.22: One of the brightest globular clusters, discovered in 1665.
messierNotes.24: The Sagittarius Star Cloud, a dense patch of the Milky Way.
messierNotes.27: The Dumbbell Nebula, the first planetary nebula ever discovered (1764).
messierNotes.31: The Andromeda Galaxy, about 2.5 million light-years away and visible to the naked eye.
messierNotes.32: A compact satellite galaxy of Andromeda.
messierNotes.33: The Triangulum Galaxy, the third-largest galaxy of the Local Group.
messierNotes.40: Winnecke 4: a faint double star that Messier mistook for a nebula.
messierNotes.42: The Orion Nebula, a stellar nursery 1,300 light-years away, visible to the naked eye in Orion's sword.
messierNotes.44: The Beehive Cluster (Praesepe), known since antiquity. Galileo was the first to resolve its stars.
messierNotes.45: The Pleiades, the Seven Sisters: a young cluster about 440 light-years away.
messierNotes.51: The Whirlpool Galaxy, where spiral structure was first recognised (Lord Rosse, 1845).
messierNotes.57: The Ring Nebula: the glowing shell of a dying star.
messierNotes.73: Not a cluster at all: just four stars that happen to line up.
messierNotes.82: The Cigar Galaxy, brightened by a burst of star formation after meeting M81.
messierNotes.87: A giant elliptical galaxy. Its black hole was the first ever imaged (2019).
messierNotes.97: The Owl Nebula, a planetary nebula with two dark 'eyes'.
messierNotes.101: The Pinwheel Galaxy, a large face-on spiral.
messierNotes.104: The Sombrero Galaxy, with a bright core and a dark dust lane.
